documents.abstract: Abstract In the wake of terrible occurrences, social media has become the preferred source for real-time information. Social media has become a significant instrument for victims of catastrophes to express their needs, document incidents, request support and share information related to their situation. However, automated analysis may be fairly difficult in the case of casual, abbreviated, grammatically inconsistent, spelling-variant and other textual noisy communications. Artificial intelligence may be used to this data to enhance the response to catastrophes provided by technology and the well-being of humans and help in the improved detection and organization of communications related to disasters. The current research is a study on the feasibility of the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) based on transformers to classify the social media postings about the tragedy with background noise. A social media dataset related to catastrophes is pre-processed adequately to develop classification models. For the comparison of the performance of the handling of textual content on catastrophes a transformer-based model and a conventional machine-learning baseline are taken into consideration. Some of the main performance indicators used to evaluate the models include accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The problems caused by casual and distracting social media text are given specific attention. This project aims to (1) describe the challenges of collecting and evaluating noisy user-generated data and (2) empirically evaluate transformer-based text categorisation in a disaster-response setting. The research explores the use of AI-driven natural language processing on social media platforms connected to catastrophes to assist in the timely comprehension of crisis-related communication and human well-being. Moreover, it adds to the greater issue of Artificial Intelligence for social benefit.

Rapid urbanization, increasing motorization, and spatial concentration ofemployment and services are putting increasing pressure on urban road networks. Trafficcongestion is not only a transportation problem, but also a multidimensional urbanplanning problem that affects travel time, economic productivity, energy consumption,air quality, road safety, and social amenity. This paper explores the relationship betweenroad infrastructure and traffic congestion, identifies the main mechanisms that causerecurrent and non-recurrent congestion, and systematizes engineering, planning, policy,and digital interventions. A literature-based analytical approach is used, combiningclassical theories of demand, network balance, and bottleneck effects with recentevidence on demand management policies, intelligent transportation systems (ITS),artificial intelligence, and integrated urban mobility. The analysis shows that increasingroad capacity alone cannot guarantee sustainable reductions in congestion, as additionalcapacity may encourage additional car traffic. Road network improvements are morelikely to achieve sustainable results when combined with adaptive traffic signalmanagement, public transport prioritization, parking and demand management,coordinated land-use planning, real-time information, and multimodal accessibility. Aconceptual framework is proposed that considers road capacity, traffic demand, networktopology, control quality, and passenger behavior as interacting variables. The paperconcludes with recommendations for developing cities, which are particularly relevantfor the rapidly developing urban centers of Central Asia.

A smart city is defined as a city that employs communication and information technologies to enhance the entire process of governance, including making it more effective, public access to data, and enhancing the quality of government services alongside the well-being of citizens. Rapid population growth creates problems for cities associated with urban transport, air pollution, energy inefficiency, water scarcity, waste disposal issues, and burden on urban infrastructure. Smart city solutions include using new technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Geographic Information System (GIS), 5G, and intelligent sensors, for efficient resource management. Smart city technologies help monitor different aspects in real time and make intelligent decisions in the areas of transport, health, energy supply, waste management, and public safety. In India, the Smart Cities Mission has made cities implement several technology-based initiatives for sustainable development and citizen engagement. In this research paper, the concept, design, technologies, applications, advantages, problems and perspectives of smart cities are examined, taking into account their applications in India.

Abstract The global community stands at a critical crossroads where technological advancement and environmental preservation must converge to ensure human well-being. This paper explores the multidisciplinary approach required to navigate global futures, focusing on the harmonization of economic science, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and digital innovation with sustainability metrics. Focusing specifically on the drought-prone Sangola Taluka of Solapur District, Maharashtra, this study examines how traditional agrarian economies can transition into sustainable models using precision farming. With over 73.96% of the workforce in Solapur engaged in agriculture, yet suffering from an average rainfall of less than 545-750 mm, integrating AI-driven resource frameworks is crucial. The paper provides factual insights into the pomegranate economy of Sangola and highlights how digital interventions can optimize water use, mitigate economic risks, and align local systems with Environmental Sustainability. Critical interventions such as IoT sensors, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for pathological tracking, and decentralized drone application systems are detailed to model an optimal input-to-output agricultural grid.

Abstract Technology has changed the way people use language and communicate with one another. The growth of the internet, smartphones, social media and artificial intelligence has brought major changes in the way we read, write, speak and share information. English, being widely used in education, business, science and international communication, has been greatly influenced by these changes. Today, communication is not limited to books, classrooms or face-to-face conversations. People communicate through emails, social media, video calls, online classes, digital presentations and AI-based tools. This paper examines the changing relationship between language, technology and communication, with special focus on English. It discusses how digital technology has influenced English language use and how artificial intelligence is becoming part of language learning and communication. The paper also looks at the advantages and problems of using AI in English education. AI tools can help learners improve their vocabulary, grammar, writing and communication skills. At the same time, too much dependence on such tools may affect independent thinking, creativity and originality. The paper argues that technology should support human communication rather than replace it. English education should therefore help learners develop language skills along with digital literacy, critical thinking, creativity and responsible use of technology. The paper concludes that preparing students for the future requires a balanced approach in which technology and human abilities work together.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a fundamental catalyst for transformation across global societies, fundamentally altering the pathways available to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This paper presents a critical, socio-technical review of AI's dual role as both an enabler and an inhibitor of sustainability. Synthesizing recent macro-level consensus frameworks and empirical case studies, we demonstrate that while machine learning architectures optimize resource efficiency, power smart grids, and augment climate tracking, they simultaneously expose systemic vulnerabilities. These include severe ecological footprints driven by the energy-water nexus of hyperscale data centers, algorithmic bias that exacerbates socio-economic inequality, and a compounding interdisciplinary 'expertise gap.' This paper maps these dual-impact nodes across environmental, social, and economic dimensions, concluding with actionable governance strategies designed to guide policy toward a balanced digital-green transition.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Abstract Industry 4.0 has brought about a paradigm shift of global production systems from traditional manufacturing to highly automated ecosystems. The pièce de résistance of this evolution is the "Dark Factory" or "Lights-Out Manufacturing", which refers to a production facility that is designed to run unattended with little to no human intervention throughout the entire process. This study investigates in the secondary data collected from industry reports, academic literature and corporate case studies contexts of dark factories technological framework, their economic potential and scalable operating aspects. Analysis uses data from 2013 to October 2025. Results indicate that fully dark factories remain a niche implementation limited mostly to high volume, high precision industries; however, "semi-dark" environments are being established based on the advances of Artificial intelligence (AI), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and advanced robotics. The study comes to the conclusion that, continuous uninterrupted production and low variable overheads cost providing the massive economic benefits to the manufacturing industries. But at the same time the management must overcome the major challenges related to the cyber vulnerabilities, large initial investments and the socioeconomic effects of workforce relocation.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and conversational technologies are revolutionizing the tourism industry's digital interactions—shaping the way we connect with travelers globally.AI and conversational technologies have dramatically changed how the global tourism industry reaches travelers digitally. One of these innovations is the use of AI-powered chatbots by Online Travel Agencies (OTAs) to transform the way consumers engage with travel platforms, turning them into dynamic, personalized, and conversational spaces for booking. This research explores the role of AI-powered conversational agents in improving customer engagement and booking conversion rates within the highly competitive tourism industry worldwide. This research highlights the cognitive and psychological factors that contribute to user trust and satisfaction, such as the ability to provide 24/7 availability, custom itineraries, and smooth payment processing, in the case of generative and hybrid chatbots. Drawing from the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) paradigm and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the paper proposes that real-time algorithmic support to address travel anxiety and perceived value of the travel experience. Furthermore, it faces industry challenges such as AI hallucinations, data privacy, and the delicate balance between automation and the human touch. The insights provide actionable strategies for online travel agencies (OTAs) and hospitality marketers looking to adopt conversational AI, improve user journeys, and secure a lasting competitive advantage in the digital realm.

Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is transforming marketing communication, with AI-generated voices emerging as an increasingly important means through which brands communicate with consumers. This paper examines AI-generated voices from a consumer psychology perspective, focusing on how consumers interpret and respond to synthetic voices used in marketing communication. Drawing on literature from artificial intelligence, marketing, consumer behaviour and human–computer interaction, the paper explores the psychological significance of vocal characteristics such as naturalness, human-likeness, prosody, anthropomorphism and emotional expression. It further examines how these characteristics can shape consumer perceptions of message credibility, authenticity and brand trust. The discussion highlights the growing use of AI-generated voices across advertising, social media, voice commerce and interactive brand communication, with selected examples from the Indian marketing context illustrating their applications in personalisation, engagement and localisation. The paper argues that the effectiveness of AI-generated voices depends not simply on technological sophistication, but on how consumers psychologically interpret the voice and its relationship with the message and brand. The paper concludes by identifying directions for future research on AI-mediated brand communication.

Abstract We saw that the parameters for a dental printing process have a significant influence on the quality of the dental printed part, such as the layer height, speed of printing, orientation of printing, exposure time, and some parameters related to the used resin. There are many tra ditional ways of choosing the parameters, which are mostly empirical, and consequently lead to errors of dimensions, flaws on surfaces, and high consumption of material; there is also high production time. An Artificial Intelligence (AI) supported optimization scheme is proposed here for the optimal selection of 3D printing parameters to increase the quality and the production efficiency of individual dental prostheses. The proposed approach consists of data acquisition, data collection/preprocessing, feature analysis, training of the machine learning models, and optimization of the parameters to find out correlation between the printing conditions and quality factors such as dimensional accuracy, surface roughness, manufacturing time and con sumption of the materials. Various performance metrics are employed to analyze the different machine learning models and then the best one is utilized to determine the optimum parameter. There are plans to minimize the trial and error methods and to select the parameters on a data driven basis.

"Major industrial accidents constitute one of the most critical risk areas of modern industrial societies due to their high destructive effects despite their low probabilities of occurrence. Cases throughout history prove that these events arise not only from technical failures, but also from organizational weaknesses, systemic deficiencies, human factors, and inadequately designed safety systems. Root cause analyses reveal that the underlying causes of accidents are the insufficient analysis of reaction kinetics, the failure to correctly evaluate the accident chain developing after the loss of control, and, most importantly, the failure to keep risk analyses up to date. This situation proves that process safety should not be limited only to engineering design; it makes a holistic approach encompassing operational discipline, human factors, and organizational learning capacity necessary. The dioxin release that occurred in the town of Seveso, Italy, as a result of the uncontrolled shutdown of a reactor and the failure to correctly evaluate the by-products that could be released, fundamentally changed the European perspective on industrial safety and paved the way for the issuance of the first Seveso Directive. The Seveso Directives established within the European Union and the Regulation on the Prevention of Major Industrial Accidents and Mitigation of Their Effects (BEKRA Regulation), which entered into force in our country in line with these directives, constitute the fundamental legal and technical infrastructure for the prevention of accidents and minimization of their damages within the scope of technological disaster management. The Bhopal tragedy, which occurred despite the first directive being in force, and the Baia Mare accident, which resulted in environmental damage crossing national borders, became milestones in industrial safety and enabled the principle of “preventability of accidents” to be replaced by a more comprehensive understanding of “risk management.” In this process, critical requirements such as the domino effect, land-use planning, and informing the public were introduced into the directives. Lessons learned from experienced industrial accidents reveal that the “prescriptive” approach alone is not sufficient in the integration of safety management systems into processes. Current requirements make it necessary to adopt a “performance-based” approach that goes beyond the set of rules. Although significant progress has been made in our country in terms of regulatory compliance, there are still areas for improvement regarding process safety culture, organizational learning processes, and the internalization of advanced risk analysis techniques. For effective accident risk management, compliance with only regulatory parameters should not be considered sufficient; a performance-based, holistic, and sustainable process safety strategy should be ensured to permeate all operational processes. It is of critical importance that future studies strengthen interdisciplinary approaches and focus particularly on safety culture and organizational learning processes."

Across modern literary history, children have served as powerful symbolic figures through which societies negotiate core social values. Yet despite their prominence in canonical criticism, we lack a systematic account of how often children appear in novels, how they are valued, and what kinds of agency they are afforded over time. To address this gap, I conduct a large-scale computational analysis of 9,544 English-language novels published between 1800 and 2000. This study provides the first large-scale extraction of child characters from the modern novel, combining classical natural language processing with large language models to measure their visibility, emotional valuation, narrative agency, and independence from kinship structures. Contrary to dominant histories of childhood, children and adolescents become progressively less visible in the novel over time, a decline driven by the erosion of the adolescent girl in particular. Children maintain a more positive emotional valence than adults even as their agency lags behind adult peers, suggesting a broader portrait of children as sentimentally valued, yet structurally constrained social actors.

The rapid development of cloud technology, big data, and artificial intelligence has changed the way data pipelines are managed in today’s world. Conventional data pipeline management systems depend on rule-based automation and manual intervention making them less effective in managing dynamic workloads, detecting anomalies, recovering from faults, and optimizing resources. The recent advances in Agentic Artificial Intelligence, LLMs, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent systems have given rise to the autonomous systems that can perform monitoring, diagnosis, recovery, and optimization on their own. This review studies the state-of-the-art AI information pipeline management processes, intelligent work flow orchestration, autonomous decision making, and self-healing systems. The paper reviews the existing methodologies, including ETL automation, metadata-based data ingestion, optimization through reinforcement learning, and agent-based orchestration systems, and presents their advantages, limitations, and potential fields of application. Moreover, the review identifies main research problems faced by researchers and developers including explainability, interoperability, scalability, security, and adaptation in heterogeneous cloud environments.

The shift from Industry 4.0 to Industry 5.0 marks a profound paradigm evolution in strategic human resource management (HRM), transitioning from pure technological automation to human-centric socio-technical synergy, sustainability, and organizational resilience. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature published between 2021 and 2026 to evaluate the influence of digital HR transformation—encompassing artificial intelligence, predictive people analytics, cloud-based HRIS, and collaborative robotics (cobots)—on multi-dimensional employee engagement (vigor, dedication, and absorption). Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) framework, 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies were systematically selected and categorized. The synthesis reveals that while digital HR transformation significantly drives operational efficiency, its direct impact on employee engagement is mediated by digital fluency, perceived organizational support, and psychological safety. Furthermore, algorithmic transparency and responsible data governance serve as critical moderators that mitigate techno-stress, privacy anxieties, and algorithmic burnout. The paper delivers an integrative socio-technical framework for Industry 5.0, offering strategic guidance for organizational leaders seeking to align cutting-edge HR technologies with human well-being and sustainable performance.

In contemporary organizational research, the imperative to balance economic productivity with human sustainability has elevated Sustainable Human Resource Management (Sustainable HRM) into a core strategic framework. This critical review systematically evaluates 16 benchmark empirical and conceptual studies published between 2021 and 2026 to investigate how Sustainable HRM practices influence tri-dimensional employee well-being (physical, psychological, and social) and long-term organizational performance. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 systematic review protocols, this study synthesizes structural equation modelling (SEM) findings, panel econometrics, and qualitative case studies across diverse industrial and geographical settings. The synthesis reveals that while traditional HRM prioritizes short-term transactional output, Sustainable HRM embeds ergonomic work design, psychological safety, work-life boundary protection, and green employee voice, yielding a significant positive effect on psychological capital (β = 0.44, p < .001) and work-family enrichment (β = 0.41, p < .001). Meta-analyzed structural models demonstrate that physical and psychological well-being fully mediate the relationship between sustainable work practices and employee job performance (β = 0.38, p < .001), while drastically reducing turnover intentions. However, critical gaps persist regarding paradoxical workload pressures under green mandates and regional implementation disparities. This paper presents a multi-level governance framework providing actionable pathways for HR leaders to operationalize sustainable well-being.

Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine – Clinical Terms (SNOMED CT) enables semantically interoperable health data, but implementation in Thailand is hindered by language and workflow challenges. We evaluated whether large language models (LLMs) can automate SNOMED CT concept extraction from Thai clinical documents. The objectives of this study are to develop a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical named entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, and to compare the performance and resource requirements of closed-source and open-source LLMs on a human-annotated dataset. The dataset was manually annotated from 220 Thai medical documents (6,390 entities) from three outpatient departments. Our retrieval-augmented framework was evaluated using four LLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4.1, Qwen 3, and MedGemma) as experimental based models which were comparatively analyzed for entity recognition using precision, recall, F1 score and concept linking using character-level metric, Intersection over Union (IoU), as well as resource consumptions. For entity recognition, Gemini achieved the highest performance (loose F1 83.31%). For SNOMED CT concept extraction ranked most similar (Top-1) by encoder models for retrieval and re-ranking, IoU scores were 39.42% (Gemini), 34.44% (GPT), 29.86% (MedGemma), and 28.62% (Qwen). Average processing time for end-to-end extraction was 5–6 minutes per document for Gemini and GPT, with cost estimates in United states dollars (USD) of USD 0.035 and USD 0.019 per document, respectively; local open-source inference required up to 10 minutes per document. This study established a proof-of-concept framework for automated clinical entity recognition and SNOMED CT concept linking from Thai medical documents, demonstrating practical LLM performance with trade-offs between accuracy, cost, and efficiency across closed-source and open-source models.

As generative artificial intelligence (GAI) reshapes business education, instructors must simultaneously safeguard academic integrity and develop students’ AI literacy for an increasingly AI-driven workplace. This study developed the GAI Learning Framework (GLF), a replicable, step-by-step experiential learning approach for case-based projects in undergraduate business courses, illustrated through an operations management (OM) application. Rather than enabling passive cognitive offloading, the GLF promotes active learning by requiring students to craft context-rich prompts grounded in course materials, systematically compare outputs across multiple GAI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini), and critically evaluate discrepancies against independently verified sources. The framework was implemented across two sections of an undergraduate OM course and evaluated using a student survey that combined Likert-scale items with open-ended reflections (n = 50). All three constructs exceeded the scale midpoint, with pooled means ranging from 3.93 (Constructive Alignment) to 4.08 (Cognitive Load/Scaffolding). Qualitative student reflections further indicated that students perceived the framework as fostering active learning, AI platform literacy, and professional communication skills. This study offers educators a practical, classroom-tested framework for integrating GAI tools into case-based projects in business courses while preserving analytical rigor and promoting experiential learning. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/ited.2026.0224 .

Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, yet susceptibility mapping in data-scarce areas remains challenging. This study proposes a reproducible Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) framework that integrates Google Earth Engine (GEE), ensemble machine learning, and explainable AI (XAI) for landslide susceptibility mapping in central Nepal. Using a balanced dataset of 9,479 observations from 4,743 landslide and 4,736 non-landslide locations, extracted seven conditioning factors: topographic (elevation, slope, aspect), climatic (rainfall), ecological (NDVI, land cover), and anthropogenic (population density) within the GEE cloud computing environment. Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models using stratified train-test splitting and 10-fold cross-validation. Both models showed strong predictive performance, with XGBoost achieving superior results (Accuracy: 88.3%, ROC-AUC: 0.952) compared to RF (Accuracy: 87.9%, ROC-AUC: 0.945). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified slope as the most influential predictor associated with model predictions followed by rainfall (16%) and elevation (15%), while lower NDVI values consistently correlated with higher susceptibility. The susceptibility map identified high-risk zones concentrated in Sindhupalchok, Dolakha, Dhading, Rasuwa, Gorkha, and Nuwakot districts. This framework reveals that freely available satellite data, cloud computing, and explainable machine learning can be effectively integrated for susceptibility mapping and community resilience initiatives.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with geospatial analysis, commonly referred to as GeoAI, provides new opportunities for renewable-energy planning and site-suitability assessment. However, limited attention has been given to integrating Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with machine learning (ML) for offshore wind farm suitability assessment. This study proposes a GeoAI framework to predict offshore wind farm suitability using ensemble machine-learning techniques. A pooled technology-aware ML model was developed using nine predictors, including a turbine type to account for fixed-bottom and floating technologies. Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression were evaluated, with a majority-class classifier included as a baseline. Model development and hyperparameter optimization were conducted using five-fold stratified group cross-validation based on geographic blocks, with weighted F1-score used as the primary model-selection metric. Gradient Boosting achieved the best model, with a weighted F1-score of 0.8077, followed closely by XGBoost (0.8031), and was therefore selected for final evaluation. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis further revealed that wind power density, wind speed, and water depth were the most influential factors governing offshore wind farm suitability predictions.

Automated crack segmentation is a key component of vision-based structural health monitoring for civil infrastructure. However, many deep learning approaches remain computationally demanding for embedded edge devices and exhibit limited generalisation across diverse materials and imaging conditions. This paper presents a lightweight deep learning architecture designed to balance segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and cross-domain robustness. The artificial intelligence contribution is an efficient encoder–decoder integrating depthwise separable convolutions, lightweight multi-scale context aggregation, and channel attention. The proposed approach targets crack continuity through a unified design for thin-structure segmentation under strict computational constraints. The engineering contribution is a practical inspection method for structural health monitoring systems with limited memory, latency, and power budgets. Experiments on a joint dataset comprising 30,017 crack images collected from 20 heterogeneous datasets demonstrate competitive performance across diverse conditions. The proposed Lightweight Attention Channel-Enhanced Crack Segmentation (LACE-Crack) architecture achieves a higher harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1 score) (0.569 vs. 0.566), precision (0.751 vs. 0.732), mean intersection over union (0.694 vs. 0.693), optimal image scale (0.489 vs. 0.480), and optimal dataset scale (0.425 vs. 0.411) than the comparison architecture, with comparable recall (0.459 vs. 0.462). It also requires approximately 43% fewer parameters and 64% fewer floating-point operations. These results demonstrate a strong balance between crack segmentation performance and computational efficiency, supporting the practical use of lightweight artificial intelligence for infrastructure inspection under deployment constraints.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: This scoping review aimed to examine the methodological characteristics and performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based speech intelligibility assessment in individuals with acquired motor speech disorders. It also evaluated the clinical applicability of AI-based assessment by reviewing the relationship between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings. Four international databases (PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect) and three Korean databases (KISS, DBPIA, and RISS) were searched up to March 2026. Fifteen studies were selected after applying predefined exclusion criteria. The selected studies were classified and synthesized descriptively without risk-of-bias assessment. 1) Reading tasks were the most frequently used speech task across the 15 included studies, regardless of the data collection method. 2) A wide range of automatic speech recognition systems (e.g., Google Cloud ASR API; Google LLC, Mountain View, CA, USA) and machine learning and deep learning models (e.g., bidirectional long-short term memory, convolutional neural networks, support vector machines, and linear regression) were used, with no single approach predominating. 3) Many studies reported strong correlations or high levels of agreement between AI-based assessments and human perceptual ratings, whereas some reported weak correlations or nonlinear relationships. The included studies generally reported positive associations between AI-based and perceptual intelligibility measures, although the performance metrics and models varied considerably across studies. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution in clinical applications.

Systematic comparisons of the classic airfoil literature with modern codes have been limited less by physics than by the labour of extracting data from scanned charts. This study shows that optical character recognition and an AI agent, working under the author’s direction, can automate this chain: source retrieval, chart calibration, visual data reading, simulation campaigns, quality control and documentation. With this workflow, all 112 section charts of NACA Report 824 and three planform figures of Hoerner’s Fluid-Dynamic Lift were recomputed with XFOIL, MSES and AVL in about 7.5 hours of elapsed time. Lift-curve slopes agree to a median +2.2 % (XFOIL), and the overprediction grows with thickness. Zero-lift angles are too negative in proportion to camber in both codes; transition modelling and tunnel-wall corrections were ruled out as causes. Drag is underpredicted by about 15 % at all Reynolds numbers. The offset vanishes for Ncrit ≈ 5, an effective parameter for surface imperfections or the shared boundary-layer model. Maximum lift is overpredicted, most for thin sections. AVL reproduces Hoerner’s planform data within a few per cent where the flow is attached and the edges are sharp. Automated checks found errors in the source, the codes and the agent’s own work; human verification remains essential.

In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are being facilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cow recognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are pretty essential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitated by cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till now for the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like the fingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, we can recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have used Yolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector of Artificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, to train a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configuration computer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get such powerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique method where we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. To eliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self- enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helps to improve performance by increasing the amount of data. However, without a large amount of data, it will be possible to predict appropriately because of the presence of self-enhancing features. This certain program helps the model to improve its capability for delivering faster responses. LLM is responsible to add the self-enhancing feature. On the other hand, to find out the most suitable Yolo model for our research, we have trained data with three different versions of Yolo: Yolo v7, v8, and v9. We evaluated the performances of these three versions in terms of Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 and found Yolo v9 to be the best among them. It excels with a precision of 0.391, a recall of 0.916, a mAP50 of 0.559, and a mAP50-95 of 0.307.

The rapid popularization of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is reshaping the communication of social visual content for luxury brands. This paper takes professionally generated content (PGC) and user-generated content (UGC) as research objects and explores changes in consumer perceptions of luxury brand visual marketing before and after AIGC intervention. Based on consumer perception theory and luxury marketing theory, the paper defines core concepts such as luxury brand visual marketing, PGC, UGC, AIGC, perceived luxury, perceived craftsmanship, and perceived trust. Taking existing studies on human-produced PGC and human-produced UGC before the popularization of AIGC as a reference, it analyzes the mechanisms and practical limitations of traditional official materials and native user content in three perceptual dimensions, and further discusses the perceptual changes brought by AIGC-assisted brand PGC, AIGC-involved user UGC, and AIGC-led visual marketing materials. The study finds that the influence of AIGC has a dual nature. It improves content production efficiency and visual expressiveness, while also affecting the human craftsmanship narrative and brand authenticity of luxury goods. Its underlying logic follows the mechanism of “production mode-value perception isomorphism” and perceptual spillover: de-humanization on the production side is regarded by consumers as a signal for judging brand value, and this signal spills over from the communication stage to the product level. While empowering communication, it continuously dilutes perceptions of the human craftsmanship value and authenticity of luxury goods. This paper clarifies the logic of perceptual evolution in luxury brand visual marketing under the AIGC environment and provides theoretical reference for brand digital communication practice and subsequent academic research.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery frequently encounters the compounded challenges of non-stationary operating conditions and small-sample data constraints. Traditional deep learning models often exhibit suboptimal performance when addressing these issues. Deep Generative Models (DGMs) offer innovative solutions by synthesizing high-fidelity data samples, reconstructing latent system states, and modeling complex multimodal data streams. This paper presents a review of rotating machinery fault diagnosis technologies based on DGMs. The state-of-the-art applications of DGMs and their variants, including Deep Autoregressive Models (DARs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Diffusion Models, and Large Language Models (LLMs), are systematically summarized. Specific applications discussed include data generation, domain adaptation and generalization, multimodal data fusion, as well as downstream fault diagnosis and anomaly detection. Furthermore, this review contrasts DGMs with traditional signal processing methods and standard deep learning models. Current limitations are also critically analyzed, focusing on parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies, interpretability (reliability), and computational efficiency for edge deployment. Finally, future research directions are proposed, emphasizing few-shot or zero-shot learning, robust multimodal data generation, physics-informed hybrid DGM architectures, and the integration of reinforcement learning with DGMs to further enhance diagnostic accuracy in practical scenarios.

With the transition toward global carbon neutrality and a circular economy, remanufacturing technologies for high-value industrial components have gained significant attention. Additive cladding processes such as laser cladding, directed energy deposition (DED), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and plasma transferred arc (PTA) are key solutions for localized structural restoration. However, dynamic melt pool instability and complex thermal histories often induce defects like porosity and microcracks, degrading product reliability. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multi-sensor monitoring and closed-loop control systems have been introduced to enhance process stability and repeatability. This review comprehensively categorizes additive cladding processes for remanufacturing and explores recent advancements in AI-driven sensing, deep-learning-based defect prediction, adaptive feedback control, and digital twin integration. Finally, critical technical challenges and future perspectives for industrial deployment are discussed.

Aquatic toxicology is rapidly evolving from conventional single-contaminant toxicity testing toward an integrated discipline capable of addressing complex chemical mixtures, emerging contaminants, climate-related stressors, and ecosystem-level responses. Aquatic ecosystems are increasingly exposed to pharmaceuticals, pesticides, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), microplastics, nanoplastics, nanoparticles, industrial chemicals, antibiotics and transformation products. At the same time, climate change, eutrophication, habitat alteration and changing hydrological conditions can modify contaminant fate, bioavailability and toxicity. Recent advances in high-resolution mass spectrometry, non-target chemical analysis, multi-omics, environmental DNA (eDNA), adverse outcome pathways (AOPs), exposomics, biosensors and artificial intelligence are transforming aquatic toxicology. Emerging research increasingly emphasizes environmentally realistic concentrations, chronic exposure, mixture toxicity, trophic transfer and interactions between chemical and non-chemical stressors. Multi-omics approaches can connect molecular initiating events with physiological and ecological outcomes, while machine learning can assist contaminant identification, toxicity prediction and risk assessment. Micro- and nanoplastics are particularly important because they can act as both toxicants and vectors for other contaminants. Future aquatic toxicology should integrate field observations, laboratory experimentation, computational modelling and real-time environmental monitoring. Standardization, validation, transparency and environmentally relevant experimental designs will be essential for translating technological advances into effective ecological risk assessment and management.

Despite the rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in language education, longitudinal practitioner-centred accounts of how teachers' instructional practices and professional competence evolve through sustained GenAI integration in Chinese cultural instruction remain scarce.This self-narrative inquiry examines one pre-service Chinese language teacher's six-month experience of integrating GenAI into adult Chinese cultural instruction at a university.Drawing on 11 reflective journals, pedagogical artefacts, and semi-structured interviews with three peer observer teachers and two professors specialising in Chinese cultural instruction, the study employs Riessman's (2008) thematic narrative analysis within Clandinin and Connelly's (2000) narrative inquiry framework.Findings reveal a developmental trajectory across three qualitatively distinct phases: designing for novelty, designing for function, and designing for integration.Concurrently, the teacher's role evolved from tool user to tool architect, with AI literacy, in-class improvisational responsiveness to technology failure, and the conceptual repositioning of GenAI from pedagogical spectacle to invisible infrastructure developing iteratively through practice.Two design principles were inductively constructed: GenAI task design should target functions irreplaceable by lowerthreshold alternatives, and GenAI-generated content should compensate for the inaccessibility of authentic materials rather than substitute for them.This study contributes a practitioner-centred, longitudinal perspective to the underexplored intersection of GenAI integration and Chinese cultural instruction, and offers empirically grounded design suggestions for instructional practice.

Based on Actor-Network Theory (ANT), this study adopts Q methodology to conduct an empirical exploration of 24 vocational education students, aiming to reveal the internal structure of their cognitive landscape. The experimental results confirm a prominent Middle Collapse phenomenon: the ideal "symmetric co-creative intentionality" is statistically completely absent, and the student group does not form a continuously progressive cognitive spectrum, but presents a drastic structural polarization. The data extract five typical factors, which are clearly divided into two camps: "defensive polarization" (rejecting the status of AI actants to defend subjectivity) and "dependent polarization" (transferring agency to technological black boxes or macro-environments). Topological analysis further shows that there are deep semantic ruptures between different cognitive groups, indicating systemic blockages in the problematization and interessement stages during the "translation" process. The conclusion of this study points out that the current human-AI collaborative cognition of vocational education students does not naturally move toward symbiosis, but is driven by skill-oriented pressure and employment anxiety, falling into an either-or "translation dilemma". This finding reveals the deep cognitive fractures that vocational education faces in cultivating “responsible co-creators” in the intelligent era, and provides key empirical evidence for reconstructing the educational paradigm of human-AI collaboration.

Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.

The spread of artificial intelligence (AI) in educational settings is transforming teaching, learning and the design of school environments (European Commission, 2022; UNESCO, 2023). Alongside the opportunities, questions have emerged regarding the teacher's educational role, which is often overlooked by approaches that focus primarily on AI literacy (Isma'il & Ibrahim, 2025). Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a teacher training model that integrates digital, interpersonal and interpretative competences. The literature highlights how teachers' attitudes towards AI depend not only on their technological skills, but also on the conceptions that shape their professional practice (Cabero-Almenara et al., 2024). Content-transmission approaches tend to be associated with greater resistance to such technologies, whilst perspectives more focused on interpersonal relationships and constructivism interpret them as tools to support learning (Chan & Tsi, 2024). Concerns regarding the spread of AI therefore involve not only technical aspects but also issues of identity linked to the meaning attributed to teaching (Puja et al., 2025). Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 347-348. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Teacher Education Between the "Frankenstein Complex" and the D-Generation.

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) prevalence rises among low- and middle-income countries where access to appropriate eye care services is lacking. Detecting DR requires retinal fundus imaging, but interpretation conventionally depends on eye-care practitioners, who are affected by shortcomings like inter-observer variability. Artificial Intelligence (AI), a promising technology for automated image examination and interpretation, enables wider, faster screening coverage and consistency. The review compares the diagnostic accuracy of AI and practitioners in detecting DR using retinal images. We conducted a systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020, searching major electronic databases with search terms: diabetic retinopathy, artificial intelligence, eye-care practitioners, and diagnostic accuracy. Eligible studies were published in English, peer-reviewed, and met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data extraction, organization, and accuracy were enabled through an Excel data form. The review included 15 of 540 identified studies. AI diagnostic tools like Google’s ARDA show equal or higher accuracy than humans in detecting DR, in some instances, in categorizing images. AI brings hope and assurance in prompt identification, management, and referral. Its performance is limited by the tendency to flag images as false positives; however, this depends on image quality, disease severity, datasets used, and overall grading criteria. Human strength remains in clinical judgement, contextualised interpretation of ungradable or low-quality images, and patient-specific management approach. AI implementation to complement care should be steered by local validation through comparison with eye care givers and approval through standardized protocols, quality control, ethical considerations, and data security.

Alzheimer's disease is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and represents one of the greatest challenges facing contemporary medicine because of its high prevalence, irreversible progression, and profound impact on patients, their families, and healthcare systems. The present study aimed to analyze recent scientific advances in the diagnosis and therapeutic strategies for Alzheimer's disease through an integrative review of specialized literature. To achieve this objective, a qualitative analysis of scientific publications was conducted. The findings reveal a significant transformation in the diagnostic paradigm, shifting from an approach based primarily on clinical assessment to one supported by biological biomarkers, advanced neuroimaging techniques, and precision medicine strategies capable of identifying neuropathological changes during the preclinical stages of the disease. Likewise, the literature demonstrates a substantial shift in treatment approaches, moving from symptomatic management toward interventions designed to modify disease progression. Important advances were also identified in the fields of artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, precision pharmacology, and the development of innovative drug discovery platforms. Although significant challenges remain regarding biological heterogeneity, clinical efficacy, safety, accessibility, and the implementation of these innovations, the available scientific evidence indicates that the future management of Alzheimer's disease will be based on early diagnosis, molecular patient stratification, and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies capable of delaying neurodegeneration and improving clinical outcomes.

Mental health systems face a persistent gap in accessible, continuous, and person-centred support. Conversational AI can expand access to psychoeducation, emotional check-ins, self-management, and service navigation, but may also introduce risks of digital exclusion, cultural mismatch, privacy concerns, unsafe advice, and overreliance on automation. This paper develops a conceptual framework integrating Orange Technology, which promotes emotional wellbeing, cultural sensitivity, social connectedness, and resilience, with empathetic AI for mental health support. An integrative literature review examined peer-reviewed systematic reviews and WHO and UN guidance published from 2021 to 2026. Evidence suggests that conversational AI can improve depression, distress, anxiety, and engagement, although effects are heterogeneous and may decline over time. Personalization and empathic interaction may enhance engagement, while the framework's effects on community resilience, cultural sensitivity, and community resource integration require further empirical validation. The framework therefore positions AI as a supportive, human-in-the-loop layer rather than a replacement for clinicians, families, peers, or communities. It connects emotional sensing, empathetic dialogue, personalized support, escalation pathways, community connection, inclusive access, and governance, while aligning mental health innovation with SDG 3, 9, and 17.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Financial stock market trend decision systems support the investment decisions by predicting future price movements and analyzing large-scale market data. Despite, IoT enabled trading systems continuously collects and exchange sentiment and market information are exposed to adversarial attacks, which misleads automated trading algorithms and results in inaccurate investment decision systems. To face this challenge, this study proposes an adversarial-resilient explainable artificial intelligence for sentiment-driven stock trading (ARXAI-SST) architecture. The proposed framework combines graph neural networks (GNN) for adversarial attack detection, FinBERT based sentiment representation, BiLSTM with attention (BiLSTM-Att) for the sentiment analysis, and SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence for enhancing model interpretability. The experimentation outcomes show that the proposed framework accomplishes higher accuracy and robustness compared with the existing approaches while providing transparent insights into the trading decisions. The proposed model offers an efficient and reliable solution for secure sentiment driven stock trading in IoT enabled financial environments.

In today's educational landscape, deeply marked by the neoliberal logic of performance and an obsession with digital self-promotion, a structural pedagogical crisis is becoming increasingly evident. Schools, traditionally understood as symbolic places of encounter, mediation and the transmission of values, now face a radical challenge: to rethink themselves, their tools and their languages in order to respond to profoundly changed educational needs. It is against this backdrop that our reflection begins, with a question intended to run through the entire discussion proposed here like a common thread: is it really possible that human beings – and, with them, educators – could be replaced by artificial intelligence in the emotional and educational spheres? And, above all, what human characteristic will no digital algorithm ever be able to replicate? The starting point for this analysis is a description of a twofold crisis affecting the contemporary world. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 277-278. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Digital Affective Literacy and Citizenship.

This article examines agentic artificial intelligence as an emerging class of technologies that fundamentally reshapes business process automation, shifting the paradigm from reactive assistant systems to autonomous solutions capable of independent planning, decision-making, and execution of multi-step actions within defined authority boundaries. The aim of this study stems from a growing realization that traditional AI implementation strategies are failing to deliver expected returns. This discrepancy between strategic ambitions and practical outcomes calls for a systematic investigation of alternative approaches to AI integration, particularly those offering higher autonomy and operational transformation potential. The study demonstrates that agentic AI fundamentally transforms the cost structure of business operations by converting variable labor expenses into predominantly fixed and highly scalable technology costs, thereby altering the economics of enterprise operations. The analysis reveals that organizations implementing agentic AI achieve dramatic operational improvements including task completion time reductions and significant cost optimizations through the elimination of manual inefficiencies. The findings further show that successful scaling of agentic systems depends not so much on technological excellence as on organizational readiness, in particular the development of appropriate governance frameworks for managing autonomous systems, ensuring transparency and explainability in automated decision-making, and integrating AI agents effectively into hybrid human-machine teams while addressing workforce skill gaps. The practical value of this research lies in providing business leaders and technology managers with actionable insights for strategic decision-making regarding AI investments, offering a systematic framework for evaluating deployment opportunities across different business functions, understanding critical success factors that differentiate successful implementations from failed pilots, and anticipating organizational changes required for effective integration. The conclusions provide direction for bridging the persistent gap between AI technological capabilities and practical business outcomes, while outlining promising avenues for future research into economic impact longer-term socioeconomic consequences of widespread AI adoption on workforce composition and organizational structures.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Abstract The emergence of autonomous AI agents, which can independently negotiate contracts, conduct financial transactions, manage customer interactions, and make business decisions with minimal human involvement, has ushered in a revolutionary era for Artificial Intelligence (AI). They promise greater efficiency and innovation, but also expose serious gaps in traditional legal doctrines of corporate liability that assume human agency, intention, and control. Recent events such as the Air Canada chatbot litigation, Robodebt in Australia, and Childcare Benefits Scandal in the Netherlands show that autonomous algorithmic decisions can lead to contract disputes, discriminatory outcomes, consumer detriment, financial loss, and institutional failures, raising fundamental questions of corporate accountability and legal responsibility. The paper seeks to critically analyze whether the existing legal framework in India, i.e., the Companies Act, 2013, the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, can deal with the liability arising due to autonomous AI agents making commercial decisions. This study adopts doctrinal, comparative, and policy-oriented legal research methods to examine emerging international regulatory approaches, such as the European Union AI Act, the OECD AI Principles, ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial Intelligence Management Systems, and Singapore’s AI Governance Framework, with a view to identifying global best practices for responsible AI governance. The paper argues that traditional fault-based liability is increasingly ill-suited to situations in which artificial intelligence systems independently influence corporate decisions. It proposes a risk-based governance framework requiring AI oversight at the board level, mandatory algorithmic audits, human accountability mechanisms, explainability requirements, and statutory reforms to embed AI governance in Indian business law. The study connects technological innovation to corporate accountability, contributing to the ongoing discussion on responsible AI regulation and offering policy recommendations to build a robust legal ecosystem that supports sustainable economic development in the Industry 5.0 era.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is rapidly becoming part of children's everyday lives, while educational research continues to highlight the persistence of widespread anthropomorphic misconceptions about AI and the limited availability of pedagogical models capable of fostering critical understanding and ethical awareness. Although Extended Reality (XR) has demonstrated considerable potential for enhancing motivation and engagement, its contribution to higher-order reflective competences remains underexplored. In particular, few studies have investigated how semi-immersive environments may promote problematization, ethical deliberation and the revision of misconceptions through aesthetic experience. Within this framework, the CAIRƐ International Research Project, developed at the University of Turin, proposes the XR Sensitive Scenario as a pedagogical framework for designing semi-immersive learning landscapes. Drawing upon Dewey's theory of aesthetic education, Montani's technoaesthetics and the experience of Studio Azzurro's Sensitive Environments, the framework conceives the virtual landscape as an educational space in which children are invited to perceive, interpret and collectively deliberate on complex socio-technological issues. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 247-248. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Digital Affective Literacy and Citizenship.

In the current educational landscape, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and gamification are progressively redefining the methods used to design and evaluate learning environments. This contribution proposes an exploratory scoping review aimed at mapping recent literature (2023–2026) on this integration, analysing its implications for inclusion, the personalization of learning pathways, and the transformations of the teacher's role. Furthermore, this study aims to move beyond a merely instrumental view of technological and didactic innovation, framing AI and gamification as educational mediators that require intentional design and methodological coherence regarding the relational and affective dimensions of educational practice. The theoretical framework is structured around three conceptual nodes: AI as a tool for adaptation (through intelligent systems, learning analytics, and generative models); gamification as a lever to promote motivation, active participation, and cognitive engagement; and inclusion as the central interpretive lens. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 341-342. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Teacher Education Between the "Frankenstein Complex" and the D-Generation.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: The introduction of generative AI into education is more than a technological shift; it poses an epistemological challenge to how knowledge is created, validated, and interpreted in formal settings. In today's hybrid "onlife" context, human-centered agency is essential to navigate an invisible algorithm-driven world. This shift brings both opportunities and tensions, highlighting profound cultural and identity considerations. Bruner conceptualizes education as an interactive process of negotiating meaning rooted in narrative thinking, which contrasts with paradigmatic, logical approaches. Narrative enables the construction of the Self by organizing lived experience into coherent plots. Generative AI, trained on vast linguistic data, fits into this framework as a dynamic dialogic mediator fostering a dialectic between human intention and probabilistic machine response, consistent with Vygotskian cultural mediation and the zone of proximal development. An exploratory questionnaire studied 127 teachers' perceptions of AI's role beyond technological acceptance, examining its mediation of narrative, introspection, creativity, and learner perceptions. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 91-92. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0. Volume DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23211262. Section: Generative AI and New Narratives of the Self.

Abstract Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly used to facilitate online group discussion, yet their influence on the affective conditions of collective interaction remains poorly understood. Existing research has largely focused on participation, efficiency, or content quality, leaving the emotional dynamics of AI-mediated deliberation underexamined. This paper investigates how AI facilitation relates to the expressed sentiment in online group discussion, understood as one measurable dimension of its affective dynamics. Drawing on two empirical studies conducted in different discussion settings in Afghanistan, one involving a rule-based facilitator and the other a large language model-based facilitator, we analyze differences in expressed sentiment between AI-facilitated and non-AI discussions. Across both datasets, participant sentiment was modestly higher under AI facilitation, although the mixed-effects analyses did not establish statistically significant condition differences. In addition, AI-generated facilitation messages exhibited higher sentiment than participant-authored messages, with a statistically reliable overall gap in both studies and a consistent direction across all five city-specific boards in the first study and all four AI-facilitated groups in the second, suggesting that AI facilitators introduced more positive affective signals into the discussion environment. Rather than treating increased positivity as an unqualified improvement, we interpret these findings as suggesting that AI systems may act as affective mediators, potentially influencing the emotional norms and tone of collective interaction. This raises normative questions about emotional regulation, power, and democratic deliberation, particularly regarding whether affective smoothing may constrain disagreement or reconfigure deliberative agency. By foregrounding affect as a dimension of AI-mediated discussion, this study contributes empirical evidence to debates on the societal implications of AI facilitation and highlights the need for greater attention to the affective norms and expressive patterns introduced by AI facilitation.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Factory accidents continue to arise from lapses that are simple to describe but hard to police continuously: a worker without a helmet, a hand inside a press envelope, a person in the path of a moving vehicle. Manual supervision and periodic audits cannot watch every station at every moment. This paper presents the AI Factory Safety Monitor (AFSM), an edge-deployed computer-vision system that analyses ordinary industrial camera streams in real time to detect missing personal protective equipment (PPE), intrusions into configurable danger zones, and unsafe proximity to operating machinery. AFSM combines a single-stage object detector, a multi-object tracker, a pose-based posture check and a rule engine that converts raw detections into graded alerts using temporal filtering to suppress false alarms. Alerts are delivered locally (beacon, siren) and remotely (MQTT, SMS, supervisor dashboard), and a compliance-analytics layer records events for audit under occupational health and safety management practice. We describe the architecture, algorithms, deployment considerations and a proposed evaluation protocol, and discuss privacy, reliability and the limits of vision-based safety as a supplement to, not a replacement for, certified safety-rated controls.
topics: Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

documents.abstract: The transition from 5G to 6G networks brings unprecedented demands for massive connectivity, ultra-low latency, and exponentially higher data rates, rendering traditional, rigid Radio Access Networks (RAN) inadequate. To manage this exponential complexity, the integration of AI into the RAN—coupled with the disaggregated, open architecture of O-RAN—has emerged as a transformative paradigm, shifting network infrastructure from purely communication-centric entities to converged compute-communication platforms. This paper presents a comprehensive survey on the integration of AI within the 6G O-RAN ecosystem, focusing on the AI-RAN manifestations (AI-for-RAN, AI-on-RAN, and AI-and-RAN) and the end-to-end Machine Learning (ML) workflows driven by hierarchical RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). We propose a novel, multi-dimensional taxonomy that categorizes AI-RAN techniques by network function, AI paradigm, target use-case, and deployment strategy. Through a detailed analysis of state-of-the-art implementations, we highlight key insights, such as the efficacy of online Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and GPU-accelerated edge computing, while identifying critical gaps, particularly the “black-box” nature of Deep Learning models that severely hinders operator trust. To address this, we emphasize the pioneering role of eXplainable AI (XAI) in achieving transparent and secure network automation. Finally, we outline open challenges such as multi-vendor interoperability and propose concrete future research directions, including Foundation Models at the telecom edge, Network Digital Twins, and Quantum ML, to realize fully autonomous, trustworthy 6G networks.

The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology has prompted global discourse on the need for a robust regulatory framework that addresses ethical, legal, and social issues and fosters the innovation through the efficiencies created by AI. This research conducts a comparative analysis of the AI governance frameworks in Japan and Indonesia, examined through the theoretical lens of Economic Analysis of Law (EAL). Japan has taken a nuanced approach that balances the dynamic development of AI with ethical oversight to uphold the Human-Centered AI Social Principles. Indonesia is in the formative stages of developing its AI regulatory environment. Through EAL, this research assesses the efficiency implications of the AI regulatory frameworks between Japan and Indonesia, looking at the implementation of AI in society. By comparing these approaches, this paper highlights the challenges and opportunities for Indonesia in regulating AI technology for the public interest. Indonesia is advised to take a multi-stakeholder approach to build consensus and engage in bilateral cooperation with Japan for the establishment of domestic legislation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Efficiency; Legislation.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: "This study introduces the metaphor of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a 'symbiote' or 'alien organism' (Floridi, 2014), drawing inspiration from the medical domain, where the integration of AI systems into the human body for therapeutic purposes requires a rigorous anthropological selection of suitable subjects."This paradigm offers the opportunity for a rereading of the pedagogical debate on the use of AI in teaching: just as the medical community identifies the subjects compatible with hosting AI for therapeutic purposes, in the same way the education system should identify rigorous and formative criteria for teachers who intend to use this technology for educational purposes. The use of AI in teaching requires a selection based on ethical and anthropological compatibility and a professional evaluation of the teacher, his pedagogical skills, his critical conscience and his educational wisdom and maturity. Chapter in: Francesco Peluso Cassese (ed.), Algorithmic Heartbeats: Affective Education in the Age of the Fourth Revolution, REN Press – Cares srl, 2026, pp. 321-322. ISBN 979-12-82860-00-0.
